investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T08:58–09:06Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" confirms zero remaining capacity on those nodes, and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms the other 4 nodes are ineligible by design. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled, preventing VM provisioning and blocking all downstream evidence collection. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-14 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain Unschedulable for the full probe timeout. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the state-polling step and produced zero evidence, violating the remote-agent-state contract which requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are configured to supply kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and both report Insufficient resources; the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every new remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a schedulable agent, and the probe times out without writing any evidence — causing the contract validation to fail with all four required fields missing (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" confirms zero remaining capacity on those nodes, and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms the other 4 nodes are ineligible by design. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled, preventing VM provisioning and blocking all downstream evidence collection. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-14 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, preventing any remote agent VM pod from being scheduled. Because the agent pod could never be created, the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity across the 2 eligible nodes (both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable, no agent VM was provisioned, and the eval runner received no response from which to extract the required evidence fields. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool in production-api; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 affinity-matching nodes is fully consumed by existing running pods, leaving no capacity for new eval-provisioned agent VMs.
[Likely] A surge or accumulation of long-running remote agent VMs from prior eval runs or user sessions has not been cleaned up, holding all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (2 out of 6) that happen to be the only nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, and those 2 nodes are at capacity — meaning even a small number of concurrent VMs can exhaust the pool.

[Possible] The 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector are not configured with kata.peerpods.io/vm support, so the effective schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

[Less likely] A node or node-pool scaling event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb eval traffic, but no node event evidence is present in the supplied packet to confirm this.
